predecessors.note: Hobson declared British sovereignty on 21 May 1840 after the Treaty of Waitangi (6 February 1840). New Zealand was legally part of New South Wales until the charter took effect on 3 May 1841.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: North and South Islands (976 cells, about 0.25 M km2 by the gazetteer). The page has no infobox area. region.text: the islands of New Zealand: the North Island by cession, the South and Stewart Islands by discovery

ledger.note: 1840: Hobson proclaims British sovereignty over New Zealand (21 May 1840). 'Hobson declared British sovereignty over the islands of New Zealand on 21 May 1840 in two separate declarations'; the North Island on the basis of cession (Treaty of Waitangi, 6 February 1840), the South and Stewart Islands on Cook's 1769 discovery. The boundary of New South Wales had been redefined to include New Zealand ('arrived from London on 15 June 1839'); the charter making a separate colony was issued on 16 November 1840 and took effect on 3 May 1841.
1841: the capital moves from Okiato (Old Russell) to Auckland, where it stays to 1865.

1842: the Chatham Islands join the colony: 'the Chatham Islands officially became part of the Colony of New Zealand in 1842.' One grid cell; the Moriori had been invaded in 1835 by Ngāti Mutunga and Ngāti Tama.

region.text: the far north of New Zealand, around the Bay of Islands

ledger.note: 1845: the Flagstaff War opens in Northland. 'The Flagstaff War took place in the far north of New Zealand, around the Bay of Islands, between March 1845 and January 1846.'

region.text: the Bay of Islands and Northland

ledger.note: 1846: the Flagstaff War ends (January 1846), after Ruapekapeka 'forcing Kawiti to retreat'.

region.text: the Waikato: 'Let Maungatautari be our boundary'

ledger.note: 1858: Pōtatau Te Wherowhero is crowned Māori king, 'in June 1858 he was crowned at Ngāruawāhia', and sets the Waikato apart: 'Let Maungatautari be our boundary.' The Crown does not recognise it; the Waikato is cut from the Crown's drawn shape, as in the maori-king-movement dossier.
1860: the First Taranaki War opens (17 March 1860): 'hostilities began on 17 March 1860'; it 'ended in a ceasefire, with neither side explicitly accepting the peace terms of the other'.
1861: the First Taranaki War ends in a ceasefire (the page gives 1861, no month).
1863: the Second Taranaki War: 'Between 1863 and 1866 there was a resumption of hostilities between Māori and the New Zealand Government in Taranaki.'

1863: Grey's invasion of the Waikato. The ultimatum was issued on 9 July 1863 and 'Troops crossed into Waikato territory three days later to begin their invasion'; the NZ Wars page: 'began the Waikato invasion in July'.
1864: the Tauranga campaign opens: 'The six-month long Tauranga campaign of 1864', culminating at Gate Pā in April.
1864: the Waikato is conquered (April 1864): 'before completing their Waikato conquest in April 1864'; the Kingite forces retreat south after Ōrākau.

1864: the Waikato is taken: 'completing their Waikato conquest in April 1864'; the Waikato is among the lands confiscated under the New Zealand Settlements Act 1863 ('1.5 million hectares of land were confiscated from tribes in Taranaki, Waikato, Tauranga and the Bay of Plenty').

region.text: the King Country behind 'the aukati, or boundary, a line of pā alongside the Puniu River near Kihikihi'

ledger.note: 1864: the Kīngitanga withdraws behind the aukati into the King Country. 'the Kingite forces retreated southwards from the Waikato after the battle at Ōrākau in April 1864'; the King Country is cut from the Crown's drawn shape. The maori-king-movement dossier records the same land as a gain from nobody.
1864: the Tauranga campaign ends with the Battle of Te Ranga (June 1864 on the page's dating): the campaign was 'six-month long'.

region.text: the East Coast: the East Cape and the eastern Bay of Plenty

ledger.counterpart: Pai Mārire forces of the East Coast
ledger.note: 1865: the East Cape War opens: 'East coast hostilities erupted in April 1865'; Carl Völkner was killed 'at Ōpōtiki on 2 March 1865'.
1866: the Second Taranaki War ends (1866) and the East Cape War ends; 'the government confiscated northern Urewera land in January 1866'.

region.text: the East Coast: the East Cape and the eastern Bay of Plenty

ledger.counterpart: Pai Mārire forces of the East Coast
ledger.note: 1866: the East Cape War ends (the page gives hostilities from April 1865 'to 1866', with the northern Urewera confiscation of January 1866).
1868: Titokowaru's War: 'War flared again in Taranaki in June 1868'.
1868: Te Kooti's War: 'Te Kooti went on the offensive from November 1868'; 'fought in the East Coast region'.
1869: Titokowaru's War ends (the page's 1868-69 pursuit of Riwha Tītokowaru).
1872: Te Kooti's War ends: he 'was finally granted sanctuary by the Māori king in 1872'; 'the last force, the Taranaki Militia, was released from service in 1872'.

region.text: the King Country (Rohe Pōtae), 'accessible to Europeans' by 1883

ledger.note: 1883: the King Country is opened to the Crown. 'by 1883 the King Country was made accessible to Europeans'; 'At a March 1883 meeting, John Bryce got a compact that allowed the surveying of the rail route'; the Main Trunk railway was begun in 1885.

region.text: the Kermadec Islands, assigned by letters patent of 18 January 1887

ledger.note: 1887: the Kermadec Islands are assigned to New Zealand. 'On 1 August 1886, HMS Diamond annexed the islands for the United Kingdom'; 'Letters patent issued on 18 January 1887, assigned the islands to the colony of New Zealand.' No grid cell.

1901: the Cook Islands are brought into the colony: 'In 1901 the islands were included within the boundaries of the Colony of New Zealand'; 'The boundary change became effective on 11 June 1901'. A British protectorate since 1888. One grid cell.
1901: Niue is brought into the colony: 'Niue was brought within the boundaries of New Zealand on 11 June 1901' by the same Order and Proclamation as the Cook Islands. One grid cell.

region.text: New Zealand with the Cook Islands and Niue as it stood in 1907

ledger.note: 1907: the Colony becomes the Dominion of New Zealand on 26 September 1907. 'The Colony of New Zealand continued until 26 September 1907'; the change 'was largely symbolic'. The Dominion is carried by the new-zealand dossier.

wars.name: Wairau Affray
wars.outcome: 'The first armed conflict between Māori and the European settlers took place on 17 June 1843 in the Wairau Valley'; no ground changed hands.
wars.note: The page extract does not name the Māori party.

wars.name: Flagstaff War

zones.text: the far north, around the Bay of Islands

wars.outcome: March 1845 to January 1846; Ruapekapeka was taken, 'forcing Kawiti to retreat'. The page gives no land change.
wars.note: Contest zone from the first campaign (March 1845) to January 1846.

wars.name: Hutt Valley campaign
wars.outcome: 'a sequel to the Wairau Affray'; Boulcott's Farm raid on 16 May 1846 and the Battle of Battle Hill from 6 to 13 August 1846. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Wanganui campaign
wars.outcome: April 1847 shooting of a minor Wanganui chief; 'A peace settlement was reached in early 1848.'

wars.name: First Taranaki War
wars.outcome: Began 17 March 1860; 'ended in a ceasefire, with neither side explicitly accepting the peace terms of the other'.
wars.note: The page gives no end month.

wars.name: Waikato War (invasion of the Waikato)
wars.outcome: July 1863 to April 1864: Ngāruawāhia taken in December 1863, 'completing their Waikato conquest in April 1864'; the Kīngitanga retreated to the King Country.
wars.note: Matches the maori-king-movement dossier's contest (1863-07 to 1864-04).

wars.name: Second Taranaki War
wars.outcome: 'Between 1863 and 1866 there was a resumption of hostilities between Māori and the New Zealand Government in Taranaki.'

wars.name: Tauranga campaign
wars.outcome: 'The six-month long Tauranga campaign of 1864', with Gate Pā in April and Te Ranga in June; land at Tauranga was among the later confiscations.

wars.name: East Cape War
belligerents: Pai Mārire forces of the East Coast
wars.outcome: 'East coast hostilities erupted in April 1865'; the government confiscated northern Urewera land in January 1866.

wars.name: Titokowaru's War
wars.outcome: 'War flared again in Taranaki in June 1868'; the pursuit of Riwha Tītokowaru ended in 1868-69.

wars.name: Te Kooti's War
wars.outcome: 'Te Kooti went on the offensive from November 1868' and was 'finally granted sanctuary by the Māori king in 1872'. The Wars page infobox: 'Crown victory. Loss of Māori land, the retreat of Kīngitanga to King Country'.
wars.note: The page also gives the settlements acts' confiscations at 1.5 million hectares (about 15,000 km2; infobox 16,000 km2) from Taranaki, Waikato, Tauranga and the Bay of Plenty; that is land title inside a colony that already claimed sovereignty, so no ledger event was made.

certainty.note: The Crown claimed all of the islands from 21 May 1840 but held little of the North Island interior; the line between Crown land and Māori land (the Waikato boundary of 1858, the aukati of 1864 to 1883, the confiscation boundaries) is approximate. Coasts are sharp.
After the King Country opened in 1883 the colony's border is the coast; the Cook Islands, Niue and the Kermadecs are fixed by the 1887 and 1901 letters patent and orders.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. Pages opened: Colony of New Zealand, New Zealand Wars, Māori King Movement, King Country, Cook Islands, Niue, Chatham Islands, Kermadec Islands, Territorial evolution of Australia (nine pages, four over the 2 to 5 budget; the Cook Islands, Niue, Chatham and Kermadec pages are one-fact pages and the Territorial evolution page is shared with the Australian colonies). The Territorial_evolution_of_New_Zealand page does not exist (URL not found).
MODEL. As with the Australian colonies the shape is legal sovereignty (the whole of the islands from 21 May 1840), with only the Kīngitanga lands cut out (Waikato 1858 to 1864, King Country 1864 to 1883) so that this dossier and maori-king-movement (oc-01) never claim the same cell. Every other Māori-held district was nominally Crown land; the wars are contests over named districts (rule 6), not changes of owner. The Crown confiscated 1.5 million hectares under the New Zealand Settlements Act 1863; that is title, not sovereignty, and has no ledger event. Counterparts of the contests that are not in the project (Northern Māori, Taranaki Māori, Tauranga Māori, Pai Mārire forces, Tītokowaru's forces, Te Kooti's followers) are written as names; none is a state held for ten years.
DISAGREEMENTS. The Colony of New South Wales page gives 1 July 1841 for the separation of New Zealand, the Colony of New Zealand page 3 May 1841. The oc-02-a dossier new-zealand starts the Dominion on 26 September 1907; this colony ends the same day. NSW's 1787 commission and the 1839 boundary redefinition covered New Zealand; not drawn in colony-of-new-south-wales.
NOT ON THE PAGES. The Treaty of Waitangi page was not opened (6 February 1840 is the Colony page's date); the provinces of 1846 and 1853 to 1876 only as names; Stewart Island and the subantarctic islands (Auckland Islands, Campbell, Antipodes, Bounty, Snares) have no dated acquisition; Tokelau is not dated on any page opened. The Cook Islands and Niue were British protectorates from 1888 and 1900 (their pages), counterpart british-colonial-empire.
GAZETTEER. All names resolve; the Kermadec Islands, the Cook Islands, Niue and the Chatham Islands are 0 or 1 cell.
